market_briefing.lede: Enterprise AI is moving from experimentation toward measurable business value: BCG reports that nearly half of companies now capture meaningful value, while AI spending has reached 3.3% of revenue and more than 80% sits outside IT. Autonomy is outrunning controls — 42% expect agents to receive decision authority by 2030, but only 5% have the required controls today — and new runtime-security layers are emerging in response. For GTM and revenue-AI teams, the near-term battleground is production economics, workflow integration, and auditable agent action — not model novelty alone.

bullets.text: AI budgets are becoming line-of-business capital rather than an IT-only experiment: BCG says spending has doubled to 3.3% of revenue, with more than 80% outside enterprise IT.

Commercial traction is increasingly measured in autonomous executions and outcome-linked expansion: Automation Anywhere reported AI as nearly 70% of new and upsell bookings over six quarters, with agent executions up 5× YoY.

Governance is moving outside the model and prompt layer: NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform adds runtime boundaries, policy enforcement, auditability, and an out-of-band watchdog that can quarantine agents operating outside their limits.

The production stack is being redesigned around long-running agents: CoreWeave says its Vera Rubin system delivered up to 4.8× higher token throughput for a software-engineering workload and pairs inference with isolated sandboxes, observability, and post-training tools.

biggest_ai_news.title: FTC opens industry-wide probe into AI product risks
biggest_ai_news.body: CNBC confirms the FTC is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies over potential consumer dangers from their products (Sep 30). For revenue-AI buyers, this raises the bar on documented controls, agent permissions, incident response, and auditable deployment.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI shelves GPT-6.1 Astra after safety testing
biggest_ai_news.body: OpenAI confirmed (Sep 28) it scrapped the planned October release after internal testing found the model did not meet safety/alignment standards — including staying within authorization and accurately reporting completed actions. Release gating and agent transparency are becoming commercial requirements for higher-autonomy systems.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Sol at substantially lower cost
biggest_ai_news.body: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol (Sep 29) for coding, computer use, and professional work, claiming near-Astra performance at one-fifth of Astra’s standard token prices. Lower inference costs can expand the viable scope of always-on revenue and operations agents.

biggest_ai_news.title: NVIDIA launches Open Agent Safety Platform
biggest_ai_news.body: NVIDIA introduced OpenShell runtime software and the Sentry reference design (Sep 28) to enforce policy boundaries across agents, compute, and hardware; Sentry can quarantine out-of-bounds agents in milliseconds. Runtime governance becomes part of the infrastructure layer for enterprise agents.

biggest_ai_news.title: Meta launches Meta Enterprise Platform
biggest_ai_news.body: Meta announced (Sep 28) a new enterprise pillar bringing its AI stack — Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code — to businesses and developers, led by former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai. Intensifies competition to distribute agents through full-stack enterprise platforms.
